commitResults.messageTitle: Guard appointment commands with assertions and logging
commitResults.messageBody:
The appointment commands and their JSON adapter had no assertions or
logging, so a broken invariant would surface only as wrong data, and
rejected input left nothing in the log.

Assert that the selected client or appointment exists before a change
and that the change took effect afterwards, including that a confirmed
deleteappt clears the undo/redo history. Assert that an appointment is
only serialised with its client, so a lost link cannot be written to
the data file as client 0. Log rejected input at FINE and in-memory
changes at INFO, by displayed reference rather than personal details.

Messages, behaviour and the data format are unchanged.

Refs #87

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a backup command for the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
The data safety feature needs a copy of the data that can be
restored later, and there was no way to take one.

BackupCommand writes the current data through JsonAddressBookStorage
into the backup folder beside the data file, using a timestamped name
or a name given with f/FILE. It calls no model mutator, so it creates
no history entry, leaves both filters alone and preserves redo.

LogicManager now skips the automatic save for it, as it already does
for appointments, since no data changed.

Refs #69

commitResults.messageTitle: Show data file problems on screen
commitResults.messageBody:
A failed load or save was only recorded in the log, and the save
failure did not name the file that could not be written.

MainApp now builds a startup notice from the data file path and the
preserved copy, and passes it through UiManager to MainWindow, which
shows it in the result box. A save failure now names the data file
path and says the last change was not saved, before the checkpoint
restores the data, both filters and the history.

Refs #69

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a restore command for backup files
commitResults.messageBody:
Restore replaces all clients and appointments with the contents of a
backup file, and the data safety feature needs it to recover from a
mistake or a hand-edited data file.

The command validates the named file as a client list before touching
the model, so a missing or unreadable file changes nothing. A successful
restore replaces the whole book through Model#setAddressBook, which
commits one snapshot, so it is undoable and earlier history stays. Both
filters are cleared afterwards so the restored list is visible.

Refs #69

commitResults.messageTitle: Publish a backup only after the write succeeds
commitResults.messageBody:
A failed write left a partial JSON file under the backup name, which
then blocked a retry because the name looked taken.

The backup is now written to a temporary file in the same folder and
moved into place only once the write has finished. The temporary file
is deleted on every path, so a failed write leaves nothing behind and
the same name can be reused.
